correctness.rationale: For symmetric weighted Laplacian L and A=λI+εL, the stationary covariance C=∫e^(-2λt)e^(-εLt)Qe^(-εLt)dt. Each (i,s) semigroup entry first appears at power ε^d(i,s), with positive shortest-path weight H_is/d!; uniform Taylor domination permits integration. Consequently C_ij leading order is m_ij=min_s(d(i,s)+d(j,s)) with factorial/binomial B_ij; C_ii has 2r_i order, yielding exact ε^(m_ij-r_i-r_j)/(2λ)^k times B_ij/sqrt(V_iV_j). No cancellations since source intensities and weights are positive. Equality r_i+r_j=m iff nearest-source sets meet; factorial log convexity and Cauchy-Schwarz give sharp unit-limit criterion and universal single-source factorial law. Boundary n>=2, λ>0, ε>0, positive symmetric weights and independent active white-noise sources are explicit. Independent rational Lyapunov coefficients on a weighted four-vertex graph verified all leading terms including disjoint-source cases; this is diagnostic, not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Bounded independent computation is corroborative only; the all-parameter proof is analytical.

value.rationale: Sparse forcing and weak migration are natural limits in spatially structured noise. The exact integer decay exponents, nearest-source sets and unit-correlation equality case provide a nontrivial, all-graph classification distinguishing vanishing variance from strongly normalized synchrony; its leading coefficient gives a concrete physically interpretable graph quantity, not an arbitrary finite instance.
residual_risks: Mathematical value is judged for the final submitted original theorem, not merely computational reproducibility.

limitations: Linearized stationary Gaussian fluctuations only, not nonlinear population positivity or extinction.
